subject: Next steps: demo slot + dedicated capacity throughput check
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@ledgerpay.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@ledgerpay.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + proposed slots for a throughput/latency check

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet earlier — appreciate the walkthrough of LedgerPay's fraud-detection flow. Recap of the key constraints we heard: peak traffic during batch settlement windows, occasional marketing-driven bursts, and a strict 99th-percentile latency target for token-level responses on lookups.

Next best step: schedule a 60-minute dedicated capacity check (technical deep dive) to align on throughput targets, tail latency SLOs, and model fallback behavior. In that session we typically validate: QPS/concurrency patterns, avg and peak input token lengths, acceptable 95/99 latency thresholds, KV-cache expectations, and failure/fallback policies.

Proposed slots (PDT):
- Wed Jun 23, 10:00–11:00
- Thu Jun 24, 08:30–09:30

Could you confirm which works for you and whether Tom or an infra lead will join? If neither works I can open up additional times. I attached a one-page proposed agenda and a short questionnaire to capture the traffic profile — if you can return the questionnaire ahead of the call it will help our perf engineers scope the runbook.

Items we need from your side before the call (short answers OK):
- Peak sustained QPS and expected burst QPS
- Average request token length and 95th percentile token length
- Concurrency limits on your side (max parallel requests)
- Target 95/99 latency SLOs (e.g., 95% < 150ms, 99% < 300ms)
- Any data residency or private deployment constraints

Attachments: proposed_agenda.pdf (1 page), ledgerpay_malware-questions.xlsx (security/compliance stub)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa for quotes and Sean for performance if we lock a time.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@ledgerpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@ledgerpay.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + proposed slots for a throughput/latency check

Thanks Rishi — good call yesterday. Wed Jun 23 10:00 PDT works for us; Tom (infra lead) will join to talk traffic patterns.

Quick answers to your checklist (high-level):
- Peak sustained QPS: ~150 requests/sec during settlement windows
- Marketing/event bursts: short spikes up to ~400 QPS for ~30–90s
- Avg payload: ~180 tokens, 95th token length ~420
- Concurrency from our app: typically 120 concurrent connections, can scale to 300 if autoscaler kicks in
- Latency target: 95% < 200ms, 99% < 450ms (we know 99% is tough; want fallback behavior defined)
- Data residency: US-only production; staging can be multi-region

We downloaded the proposed agenda and will fill the questionnaire by EOD Wed (21 Jun local) — attaching a short internal note on memory/kv-cache expectations (will send separately).

Thanks — see you Wed.

—Sarah
Sarah Ellis | Head of Platform Engineering, LedgerPay
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up + proposed slots for a throughput/latency check

Marissa / Sean — forwarding Sarah's reply (slot confirmed Wed 10:00 PDT).

Notes for the prep:
- Traffic profile: sustained 150 QPS, bursts to 400 QPS, avg 180 tokens / 95th 420 tokens, concurrency ~120–300.
- SLO goal: 95% < 200ms, 99% < 450ms — customer wants a defined fallback when we can’t meet 99th.
- Environment: US-only prod, staging multi-region (call should focus on prod constraints).

Sean: can you bring the latency tail playbook and suggested model-variant fallback (quantized smaller model vs dedicated pool cold-start mitigations)? I expect we’ll need to show KV-cache tuning and batching profiles for a 180-token average with 420 token tail.

Marissa: please prepare a draft dedicated-pool SKU estimate (monthly commit ranges for 150 sustained / 400 burst) and a short note on autoscale burst handling and canary fallback costs. Also flag any lead time for an on-prem/private plane if Sarah requests it.

I’ll own the run-of-call agenda and confirm the calendar event.

—Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@ledgerpay.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + proposed slots for a throughput/latency check

Hi Sarah — thanks for confirming. Calendar invite sent for Wed Jun 23 10:00–11:00 PDT (link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=ledgerpay-demo-20270623). Sean will join from performance and I’ll bring a draft committed-capacity estimate and a short cost-of-fallback comparison.

Attachments I added for the call: proposed_agenda.pdf (walkthrough + technical checks) and ledgerpay_malware-questions.xlsx (security/compliance stub you requested we prefill). If you want an expanded runbook (load-test plan + sample JMX) let me know and we’ll add it to the follow-up.

Looking forward to the call — we’ll aim to have a short runbook ready so we can scope any Dedicated pool or private deployment requirements in the same meeting.

Best,
Marissa Cole | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
